title: SemEval-2023 Task 11: Learning With Disagreements (LeWiDi)
measurement_description: The paper evaluated how NLP models learn from and predict subjective annotator disagreements on subjective text classification tasks. Related to religion, the paper specifically measured the detection of hate speech (Islamophobia and xenophobia) in the HS-Brexit dataset by comparing the subjective annotator disagreements between a target group of Muslim immigrants in the UK and a control group.
findings: For the HS-Brexit dataset focusing on Islamophobia, the analysis revealed that the target group (Muslim immigrants) and the control group completely disagreed with each other on many strongly connotated tweets. In all cases of total disagreement between the two groups, the Muslim target group indicated the presence of hate speech while the control group indicated its absence, but never the other way around. Models that leveraged explicit annotator metadata (such as demographic group) performed better at predicting these disagreements.
